sentences.text: Learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is carrying on business of manufacturing of Starch and Sago from Cassava Tubers (Tapioca Roots) in the name and style of ''Sri Venkatachalapathy Sago Factory'', a Small Scale Industry.

The Cassava Tubers (Tapioca Tuber),
an agricultural produce is subjected to several cleaning process including the process of making pulp by crushing and then sifting it to get starch of fine quality to manufacture the end product known as ''Tapioca Sago''.
It is totally a wet process, until the stage of making globules from wet tapioca starch for roasting and then drying to get unpolished Sago.

3. The learned Counsel for the petitioner further submitted that all Micro and Small Scale Industries including the petitioner herein numbering about 300 in the State of Tamil Nadu used to store required wet starch for home consumption in ground level feeding troughs constructed using Granite/boulder stones.
This process of cleaning impurities from wet Tapioca Starch by adding additives and using presser pumps is in vogue in Tapioca Sago manufacturing Industry since the year 1997.

Without knowing the practical procedure being followed in all over the State of Tamil Nadu by 300 Small Scale Industries, the impugned notice dated 7.5.2018 has been issued against the petitioner directing the petitioner herein to dismantle immediately Presser Pump Motors used for removing naturally occurring impurities like dirt assimilated from the raw materials Cassava Tubers, degenerated fibre, nice and immature starch etc. found in the partly processed wet Tapioca Starch meant for manufacturing Tapioca Sago.

Apart from the direction to dismantle the processing equipments, the 2nd respondent herein has issued other directions, such as, installation of additional Camera at strategic points of the factory to monitor manufacturing process, stainless steel plate to cover the floor and side walls of feed troughs used for storing wet Tapioca Starch in liquid/Solid form required for manufacturing Tapioca Sago and poly chromate sheet to form a room like structure over the feeding troughs.

4. The learned Counsel for the petitioner further submitted that such directions are issued with an ulterior motive to curtail the Tapioca Sago production of the petitioner and other Micro and Small Scale Units with a view to help vested interests in the Sago Manufacture Sector to get inflated price for their Tapioca Sago Stocks accumulated for the past 2 years awaiting abnormal price increase to make quick money.

5. The learned Counsel also submitted that the petitioner preferred an appeal to the 1st respondent herein under Section 32(4)(a) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 against the Improvement Notice dated 7.5.2018 of the 2nd respondent and the same is pending along with a Stay Petition.

But without deciding either the appeal or the stay petition, the 2nd respondent has subsequently issued similar directions on 28.5.2018 to all Sago Manufacturers including the petitioner to dismantle the presser motor pumps and to keep the seized stock and equipments in his safe custody until further order which would result virtual closing down of small scale industry of the petitioner which is the only source of his income.
6. I find some merits in the said submission of the learned Counsel for the petitioner.
7. It appears that along with the appeal, the petitioner has also filed a Stay Petition before the 1st respondent.

But without passing any orders either in the appeal or in the Stay Petition, the K.Perumal vs Commissioner Of Food Safety And Drug on 20 June, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72877487/

Therefore, this Court, without touching the merits of the matter,
hereby directs the 1st respondent, namely, Commissioner of Food Safety and Drug Administration Department, Chennai-6 to consider the pending appeal of the petitioner along with the Stay Petition and pass appropriate orders on merits and in accordance with law without being influenced by any of the observations made by this Court.

entities.text: Commissioner of Food Safety and Drug Administration Department, Chennai-6
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: Needless to say that the respondents need not take any coercive steps until any order is passed either in the appeal or in the stay petition.
8. At this stage, the learned Counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is prepared to give any undertaking for maintaining utmost hygienic condition in the factory.
This Court is of the view that it would also be looked into by the 1st respondent while considering the appeal filed by him.
9. With the above observation and direction, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
No costs.
Consequently, connected Miscellaneous Petitions are closed.
